g.text: CAUCHY RESIDUE THEOREM & REAL DEFINITE CONTOUR INTEGRALS
Residue Evaluation Arsenal // Cauchy Residue Theorem // Real Trigonometric Integrals // Improper Semicircular Integrals
Simple pole formulas // Rational function shortcut P/Q' // Higher order poles // Essential singularities
METHOD 1B: RATIONAL FRACTION SHORTCUT P(z) / Q(z)
Valid when P(z₀) ≠ 0, Q(z₀) = 0, and Q'(z₀) ≠ 0. (FASTEST GATE METHOD!)
Res(f, z₀) = [1 / (m-1)!] limᶍ→ᶍ₀ dᵐ⁻¹/dzᵐ⁻¹ [(z - z₀)ᵐ f(z)]
⚠ For double pole (m=2): Differentiate ONCE, divide by 1! = 1.
Res(f, z₀) = (1 / 2) limᶍ→ᶍ₀ d²/dz² [(z - z₀)³ f(z)]
Divide by 2! = 2 after taking second derivative!
PREPFUSION CLASSROOM DRILLS: RESIDUES OF HIGHER ORDER POLES
DRILL 1: f(z) = tan z AT z = π/2
f(z) = sin z / cos z = P(z) / Q(z)
Every pole z = (2k+1)π/2 of tan z has residue -1!
Pole of order m = 2 at z = 0.
Global contour formula // Sum of enclosed residues // Residue at infinity theorem
Where z₁, z₂, ..., zᵐ are ALL isolated singularities strictly INSIDE contour C
1. Contour C MUST be traversed in the counterclockwise (positive) direction.
2. If traversed clockwise: Multiply final result by -1.
3. Singularities OUTSIDE C or ON C (unless indented) contribute 0 to the sum.
RESIDUE AT INFINITY & TOTAL RESIDUE THEOREM
Also equals: Res(f, ∞) = - (1 / 2πi) ∮ᶜ f(z) dz (over large circle)
THE TOTAL SUM THEOREM (GLOBAL RESIDUE ZERO THEOREM):
★ For large contours enclosing all poles: ∮ f(z) dz = -2πi Res(f, ∞)!
PREPFUSION SLIDE DRILLS: SUM OF RESIDUES INSIDE SPECIFIED DISKS
DRILL 1: SUM OF RESIDUES OF f(z) = tan z INSIDE |z| = 5
Poles of tan z occur at z = (2k + 1) π/2 ≈ ±1.57, ±4.71, ±7.85...
Residue at EACH pole is -1 (from Drill 1).
Both poles z = 1 and z = 2 lie inside |z| = 3.
03. REAL TRIGONOMETRIC INTEGRALS ∫₀²ᵖ R(cos θ, sin θ) dθ
Unit circle transformation z = eᵢṤ // Standard substitution dictionary // Definite integral evaluation
Transform real integral over [0, 2π] to contour integral around unit circle |z| = 1:
SUBSTITUTION RULES (z = eᵢṤ, dz = i eᵢṤ dθ):
★ Transformed integral becomes a standard rational contour integral: ∮ᶦ᷌ᶦ₌¹ f(z) dz!
CLASSICAL DRILL: I = ∫₀²ᵖ [1 / (a + b cos θ)] dθ (a > b > 0)
Substitute cos θ and dθ: I = ∮ [1 / (a + b(z²+1)/2z)] (dz / iz)
Roots of b z² + 2a z + b = 0: z = [-a ± √(a² - b²)] / b
Product of roots = 1. Only root z₁ = [-a + √(a²-b²)]/b lies INSIDE |z|=1.
INTERVAL CONVERSION SYMMETRY RULES (FOR [0, π] AND [0, π/2])
If integrand f(θ) is symmetric about π (i.e. f(2π - θ) = f(θ)):
Holds for functions containing only cos θ or even powers of sin θ.
If integrand is an even function of both cos θ and sin θ:
Use double-angle relations cos²θ = (1 + cos 2θ)/2 to simplify before converting!
★ Avoids manual substitution into higher degree Laurent polynomials.
04. IMPROPER REAL INTEGRALS ∫₋∞∞ f(x) dx & JORDAN'S LEMMA
Upper half-plane contouring // Semicircular arc decay // Fourier and rational integrals
Conditions: Q(x) ≠ 0 for all real x, and deg(Q) ≥ deg(P) + 2:
Summed ONLY over poles in UPPER HALF-PLANE (Im(zᵏ) > 0)!
Proof: Semicircle arc Γᵗ has length πR and |f| ≤ M/R² ⇒ ∫ᶐᵗ → 0 as R → ∞.
Poles at z = ±i. Only z = +i is in UHP (Im > 0). Res at i = 1/(2i).
Integral = 2πi · (1 / 2i) = π (Matches standard arctan(∞) - arctan(-∞) = π!)
If f(z) → 0 uniformly as |z| → ∞ in UHP, and a > 0:
Requires only deg(Q) ≥ deg(P) + 1 (1 power weaker than rational!)
∫₋∞∞ f(x) cos(ax) dx = Re [ 2πi · ∑ Res( f(z) eᵢᵃ᷂, zᵏ ∈ UHP ) ]
∫₋∞∞ f(x) sin(ax) dx = Im [ 2πi · ∑ Res( f(z) eᵢᵃ᷂, zᵏ ∈ UHP ) ]
Famous result: ∫₀∞ (sin x / x) dx = π / 2 (Dirichlet integral via indented contour)
